title: 〜だけ "only / just"
meaning: Limits to a quantity or thing (neutral tone).
simpleExplanation: だけ means "only / just" in a neutral way: 学生が一人だけいます = there is only one student (a plain fact). It follows nouns and numbers (日曜日だけ, 一人だけ), verbs (見るだけ), and adjectives. だけ can replace が and を, or come before other particles (先生にだけ = only to the teacher). Unlike しか〜ない, it does not suggest that the amount is too little.
whenUsed: Stating limits and exceptions plainly: only on Sundays, just looking, only for members. Used everywhere. When you want to complain that something is not enough, switch to しか〜ない. できるだけ (as much as possible) is a set phrase.
formation: Noun / number + だけ: 一人だけ, 日曜日だけ
V-plain + だけ: 見るだけ, 見ただけ
い-adjective + だけ: 安いだけ
な-adjective + なだけ: 便利なだけ
Particles: だけが / だけを (or だけ alone), にだけ / とだけ

examples.ja: 教室には学生が一人だけいます。
examples.reading: きょうしつには がくせいが ひとりだけ います。
examples.en: There is only one student in the classroom.
examples.note: Number + だけ: a neutral count.

examples.ja: 見るだけで、買いません。
examples.reading: みるだけで、かいません。
examples.note: V-dictionary + だけで: just looking, nothing more.

examples.reading: にちようびだけ やすみです。
examples.en: Only Sunday is a day off.

examples.ja: この店は会員だけ入れます。
examples.reading: このみせは かいいんだけ はいれます。
examples.en: Only members can enter this shop.
examples.note: だけ replaces が on the subject.

examples.ja: 分からないときは、できるだけ早く先生に聞いてください。
examples.reading: わからないときは、できるだけ はやく せんせいに きいてください。
examples.en: When you don't understand, ask the teacher as soon as possible.
examples.note: できるだけ = as … as possible.

similarGrammar.difference: しか needs a negative verb and implies insufficiency. だけ is neutral.
ばかり means "nothing but" with a critical tone. だけ simply limits.
Looks similar but means "just did"; unrelated to "only".

commonMistakes.wrong: 財布に百円だけしかない。
commonMistakes.right: 財布に百円しかない。/ 百円だけある。
commonMistakes.why: Do not stack だけ and しか; choose one.
な-adjectives take な before だけ.

commonMistakes.wrong: 先生だけに言った。(meaning "said it only to the teacher", where にだけ is intended)
commonMistakes.why: Both orders exist, but にだけ clearly limits the receiver; だけに can also mean "precisely because" at N2, so the N4 answer is にだけ.

usageNotes: だけ after a number is the plain way to count a limit: 二つだけ買った.
V + だけで = "just by doing": 見るだけで分かる (you can tell just by looking).
だけじゃなく〜も (not only… but also) is a common extension.
jlptTips: If the verb after the blank is affirmative, しか is impossible; choose だけ. If it is negative and the meaning is "only", choose しか.
だけ + で (見るだけで) and できるだけ are frequent set-phrase items.
